full.description: This image is a diagram illustrating the comparison between two forms of cell death, necrosis and apoptosis. The left side (A) depicts the steps of necrosis, showing cellular swelling, membrane breakdown, and inflammation. The right side (B) depicts apoptosis, characterized by cell shrinkage, chromatin condensation, and the formation of apoptotic bodies. It serves as a comparative schematic for cellular pathology.

blind.description: This is a microscopic image of a tissue sample. It displays a fully formed granuloma characterized by a central area of granular caseation necrosis. The necrotic center is surrounded by epithelioid cells, Langhans giant cells, and a peripheral rim of lymphocytes bounded by fibroblasts. These findings are classic histological features of a granulomatous inflammation, most commonly associated with tuberculosis.

random.description: This image is a comparative diagram illustrating two distinct pathways of cell death. The left side depicts necrosis, showing cellular swelling, organelle breakdown, and eventual membrane rupture. The right side shows apoptosis, characterized by cell shrinkage, chromatin condensation, and the formation of apoptotic bodies. It serves as a visual educational tool in pathology to contrast the morphological changes of these cellular processes.
